To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antimutagenic capabilities of probiotic lactobacilli and bifidobacteria were dependent on growth phase and the type of mutagen tested.
the extracellular antimutagenicity of probiotic bacteria against two mutagens was dependent on growth phase and bacterial species.
the extracellular antimutagenecities of selected probiotic strains of lactobacillus and bifidobacterium as a function of bacterial growth phase varied with the type of mutagen used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antimutagenic effects of selected probiotic lactobacilli and bifidobacteria.
the antimutagenic effects of selected strains of Lactobacilli and Bifidibacterium as a function of bacterial growth phase and type (chemical) of mutagen.
the development of new probiotic strains with antimutagenecic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antimutagenic response of bacterial supernatants was associated with growth phase, bacterial species, and type of mutagens tested.
the antimutagenic response was dependent on the growth phase, the strain, the mutagen, and the type of bacterial genus.
the extracellular antimutagenicity of probiotics against BaP or SA was not consistent and depended on the type of mutagen and the growth phase of the bacterial strains tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antimutagenic response of the bacterial supernatants was dependent on both the growth phase and the type of mutagen tested.

the supernatants from B. adoleascentes ATCC 15702 and B. breve ATTC 15700 exhibited a higher percent of inhibition of BaP mutagenesis in the exponential phase while the supernatants of L. acidophilus ATCC 4356, L. sakei 23k and B. breve 15700 exhibited the highest antimutagenicity to SA in the stationary phases.
antimutagenic effects are not a general characteristic of all probiotics and are dependent on bacterial growth phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antimutagenic response of bacteria is not only strain specific but also dependent on the growth phase and the type of mutagen tested.
the antimutagenic response of probiotic strains is dependent on the bacterial strain and growth phase.

the extracellular antimutagenicity of probiotic bacteria is a dynamic and complex process which can be influenced by the growth phase of the bacteria, the type of mutagen and the type of bacterial species.
